criteria.criterion: (1) Grouped-CV gain over v3 at matched EXE FPR, clearly outside noise
criteria.evidence:
I reproduced compare_v3_v4.json with a scratch replica (v3 TPR 0.6252 identical; v4 0.7545 vs 0.7536; EXE FPR 0.982% for both).
- All 50 paired folds favour v4: mean +12.9 pts, sd 5.3, min +1.5. At matched 1% FPR, 49/50 favour v4 and 0/50 favour v3.
- Family-cluster bootstrap of the TPR difference (38 families, 349 malware): mean +12.96, 95% CI [+7.79, +18.25], P(<=0)=0. Dropping any single family leaves at least +11.6.
- Product-cluster bootstrap of the EXE FPR difference: [-0.47, +0.45] pts.
- Caveat: the whole gain is on goodware2-dev EXE rows (+12.9 pts). On corpus+local EXE goodware it is about zero: +0.4 at 1% FPR, -1.2 at 0.5%, +1.3 at 2%. On DLLs it is -0.5.
- Dropping the 454 dev rows that have cross-name aliases keeps the gain at +12.4 (matched +12.8).

The integrity verifier returned FAIL.
- train_rf_v4.build() appends 140 recent_train goodware rows with no holdout or fold filter. 4 sealed holdout-eval products (notepadplusplus.install, bleachbit.install, foobar2000, maven) were trained on by rf_v4 and by all 5 CV folds. This affects 6/591 holdout files (4 EXE); the hashes differ, so the leak is product-level, not identical files.
- Cross-name aliases add 7 more products, for 11 products / 26 files / 20 EXE in total. 9 of those files were seen only by v4.
- No hash-level leak, no grading-hash overlap and no Sysinternals rows were found.
- Impact is small: excluding the 4 leaked products the holdout result is still 43/461 for v3 vs 3/461 for v4.

criteria.criterion: (3) Sealed-holdout goodware FPR for v4 not worse than v3; EXE FPR not above ~1.5%
criteria.evidence:
Sealed holdout: 291 products, 465 EXE, run through Ensemble.analyze. I confirmed the ML false-positive counts from dataset/work/exp/v{3,4}_goodware2_holdout.jsonl.
- v4 EXE FPR: 3/465 = 0.645% (Wilson95 0.22-1.88%).
- v3 EXE FPR: 43/465 = 9.25%.
- Paired: 40 false positives are v3-only, 0 are v4-only; McNemar p=1.8e-12.
- Caveats: the Wilson upper bound exceeds 1.5%. The holdout comes from the same GitHub/Chocolatey pipeline v4 trained on, so it is in-distribution for v4 and new to v3.

criteria.criterion: (4) No robustness regression > 5 pts on any attack
criteria.evidence:
I reproduced the verifier's numbers from per-sample scores. At deployed thresholds (v3 4.1099, v4 3.7668), v4 minus v3 per attack:
- overlay_64k -5.4, overlay_1m -7.7, overlay_4m -9.2, strings_10k -9.2, section_inject -8.3, cert_blob -5.4.
- Within margin: header_copy -3.4, clean -4.6.
- All losing attacks have McNemar p <= 9e-4.

Diagnostic only (thresholds tuned on the holdout): at matched holdout EXE false-positive counts k=3/5/10/20, v4 beats v3 on every attack by +7 to +22 pts. The regression is therefore an artifact of the operating point: v3's TPR is bought with 9.2% FPR. The criterion as pre-registered still fails, and v4's attack-induced drop from its own clean TPR is larger (overlay_4m -12.0 vs -7.4 pts).

criteria.criterion: (5) Container gates on arm64 and amd64 (build <=300 s, ready <=25 s, replies <=5 s, no benign overruns)
criteria.evidence:
- Build: 56 s (arm64) and 46 s (amd64). Ready: 3.7 s and 7.9 s. Unit tests 50/50 pass.
- The server is OOM-killed (exit 137) under -m 1g on benign files of 62-67 MB: 3/3 runs on arm64 (DevHub, 62.6 MB) and on amd64 (Git, 66.8 MB, even as the only request). Every later request gets connection refused.
- The 2x2 test isolates the cause to the v4 serving code (vectorized _strings_raw), not the v4 models. I confirmed by reading the code: a second full bytes copy, a lowercased copy, file-length temporaries, and int64 run-index arrays.
- The frozen v3 code survives but overruns 4.0 s on 2-3 of the 6 largest benign files (answers 1), and once took 5.569 s.

methodology_flaws: The dev-pool gain is not general, and it is not independent of the holdout result. EXE goodware sets the threshold, and 1,051 of the 1,476 fit-set EXE goodware rows (71%) are goodware2-dev, from the same GitHub-releases/Chocolatey pipeline that v4 trains on (other products) and that v3 never saw. Restricting the matched-FPR comparison to the older corpus+local EXE goodware (n=425), v3 vs v4 is 0.876 vs 0.880 at 1% FPR, 0.825 vs 0.814 at 0.5%, and 0.898 vs 0.911 at 2%. On DLLs it is 0.961 vs 0.957. The 13-pt 'TPR at matched FPR' is the same effect as the holdout FPR reduction, seen from the TPR side, so it is not a second confirmation.

There is mild selection on evaluation rows. Before the holdout was sealed (12:28-12:29, before the 13:30 seal), v3 was evaluated on 205 files from 91 goodware2 dev products: dataset/work/exp/g2_dev_groups_partial.json, and the old v3_goodware2_holdout.jsonl, now backed up in scratch. That run had 6 false positives in 173 EXE. These products are dev-side (0 in the holdout), but they are among compare_v3_v4.py's evaluation rows, and the v4 recipe was designed to fix exactly those false positives (see the train_rf_v4.py docstring). The sealed holdout guards against this.

'v3 recipe' in compare is not deployed v3. Its fusion and threshold are refit on the v4 dev pool, so the 0.625 TPR is not v3's real operating point: the deployed thr 4.11 runs at 9.2% EXE FPR on the holdout. This is correct for a recipe comparison, but the result must not be quoted as 'v3 TPR'.

compare_v3_v4.py reports only fold means. It gives no paired or cluster-level uncertainty, and its printed ± is a per-fold SD of about 0.058, which overstates the noise on the difference. I added paired and clustered statistics: all 50 paired folds favour v4, and the family-cluster bootstrap 95% CI is [+7.8, +18.3] pts.

The 140 recent_train goodware rows are trained in every rf fold (and in rf_adv), so 33 fusion-fit goodware rows keep group-contaminated r scores. Both r3 and r4 are affected, so the effect is symmetric, small, and does not favour v4.

Products under two names (choco: vs github:) are not merged by norm_group(). In the dev pool I found 13 such name pairs covering 454 fit-set goodware rows (138 EXE): 454 rows are exposed to v4 training through an alias in another fold, versus 31 for v3's f3. Dropping them leaves the gain at +12.4 pts (matched +12.8), so this is not a material driver here. In the holdout it contaminates 26 files.

Fusion CV folds are stratified by row, not grouped by product, and the matched-FPR metric uses an oracle quantile on the test fold (about 295 EXE goodware per fold, so 1% is about 3 false positives). Both are symmetric across recipes and only add noise.

On the malware side: 349 samples from 38 families, with recent_train/recent_test split at random within each family. The r members are therefore family-in-sample and the f members family-grouped; this is the same for both versions. Serving-path malware TPRs (v3 87.7%, v4 83.1%) are optimistic for both, because both final ember_ft models saw all live malware.

Checked and not a flaw: r4 malware scores are the mean of 5 fold forests (500 trees) while the deployed model is one 100-tree forest. Substituting any single fold forest gives TPR 0.746-0.765 against 0.754 for the mean, so there is no inflation. Folds are identical across recipes (same fm/fg, and fusion folds depend only on y and exe), and the threshold rule and target are identical.
honest_claims:
**What can be claimed:**
- **Goodware FPR:** on product-disjoint goodware from the same GitHub-releases/Chocolatey distribution, v4 cuts unsigned EXE goodware FPR from 9.2% (43/465) to 0.65% (3/465). This is paired on identical files (McNemar p=1.8e-12), and the product-cluster bootstrap difference is -11.6 to -5.9 pts.
- **Dev-pool TPR:** on identical dev-pool rows with identical folds and threshold rule, the v4 recipe gives +12.9 pts TPR (0.625 to 0.754) at about 0.98% EXE FPR on 349 recent malware. That is outside noise: 50/50 paired folds favour v4, and the family-cluster 95% CI is [+7.8, +18.3]. The gain comes from v4 no longer flagging goodware2-style EXEs.
- **Robustness at matched FPR:** in a diagnostic with holdout-tuned thresholds, v4's attacked TPR exceeds v3's on every attack, by 7 to 22 pts.

**What cannot be claimed:**
- **General improvement:** on older corpus+local EXE goodware the matched-FPR TPR is unchanged (+0.4 pts at 1%, -1.2 at 0.5%), and on DLLs it is -0.5.
- **More malware caught at deployed thresholds:** v4 catches fewer, 83.1% vs 87.7% on recent_test without duplicates (p=0.005), with absolute numbers optimistic for both.
- **More robust as deployed:** at deployed thresholds v4 loses 5.4-9.2 pts on 6 of 7 attacks, and its drop from its own clean TPR is larger.
- **Holdout EXE FPR proven below 1.5%:** the Wilson upper bound is 1.88%.
- **Leak-free holdout:** 26 files from 11 products are contaminated, 6 by a real leak through recent_train in rf_v4.
- **Deployable:** the v4 container is OOM-killed on 62-67 MB benign files on both architectures, a serving-code bug in _strings_raw.
- **Course grading set:** it was never accessed, so nothing can be said about it.

**Files:**
- Comparison replica: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-seshadithyasaravanan-Desktop-CSCE-704-Model/73377e24-1741-4df2-9957-1d5ab9c3b7b4/scratchpad/review/judge/replicate_compare.py and replica_compare.json

Nothing under defender_product/, submission/, dataset/tools/ or live_cache/ was modified. No PE was executed, and no git operations were run.

Minor: recent_train goodware duplicates meta_goodware rows, so in the exported rf_v4 the 136 non-holdout ones are counted twice (once as a live row with stratum-balanced weight, once as a recent_train row).

Context, not a leak: recent_train/recent_test is a random split within each malware family, not by date; all 349 fusion malware come from families also in recent_train. v3 ember_ft was trained on unfiltered meta_goodware + meta_local, so v3 also saw some holdout products (e.g. other npp versions).

issues: CONCERN trigger: eval_v3.py's 8-process-pool timing has 5 v4 holdout files over 4.0 s (max 7.010 s, Winhance.Installer.exe 64.5MB). v3 has 8 (max 7.819 s). In single-process re-timing none of the same files exceeds 4.0 s (v4 worst 1.940 s, v3 2.488 s), so the overruns are mainly from CPU contention. On a slower 1-vCPU container, or with DF_WORKERS=2 running two requests at once, files of 40 to 65 MB could still overrun and be answered 1 (a false positive). This affects both versions equally and is not caused by v4.

v4 holdout EXE FPR passes the 1.5% bar on the point estimate (0.645%), but its Wilson95 upper bound is 1.879% (non-MS EXE 1.933%). With 465 EXE files the holdout cannot show the true rate is under 1.5% with 95% confidence.

The holdout comes from the same GitHub-releases/Chocolatey collection pipeline as v4's new training data (the other 70% of products). issues: CRITERION VIOLATED: v4 loses more than 5 TPR points against v3 on 6 of 7 attacks: overlay_64k -5.4, overlay_1m -7.7, overlay_4m -9.2, strings_10k -9.2, section_inject -8.3, cert_blob -5.4. Under the pre-registered rule, v4 must not replace v3.

The losses are real, not noise. In the paired test every losing attack has McNemar p<=9e-4, and its bootstrap 95% CI lies entirely below zero. v3-only detections outnumber v4-only detections by roughly 4:1 to 7:1.

Root cause, in two parts: (1) Lower operating margin. The clean efr margin fell from 4.96 to 3.86 and clean TPR fell 4.6 pts. rf_v4 scores fewer of these malware above 0.5 (0.849 vs 0.941). This follows from training on about 11k extra live goodware and from a fusion fit on a larger, harder goodware pool (EXE goodware 1,476 vs 432). (2) Real extra fragility. The refit fusion moved relative weight from the overlay-invariant NFS member r to the EMBER-based f member (f/r coefficient ratio 0.49 vs 0.36), and ember_ft_v4 is somewhat more overlay- and strings-sensitive. Even with v4's threshold shifted to match v3's clean TPR, strings_10k is still -5.2.

The 'v2_tpr' column in robustness_v4.json is not the deployed v2 baseline. eval_robustness.v2() calls the variant's own _rf_member, so for v4 it applies the v2 coefficients to rf_v4, not rf_adv. That is why it reads 0.774 clean versus 0.814 in the v3 file. Do not cite it as 'v2'.

The 'max latency' column printed by eval_robustness.py (up to 7.33 s for v4) was measured with 8 parallel worker processes, and each timing also includes the separate v2() rescoring. It is not a measurement of the 1-CPU container's 4 s budget and should not be read as one.
As the task notes, both ember_ft members trained on these 349 malware, so absolute TPRs are optimistic for both models. Only the v3-vs-v4 delta is meaningful.

Possible next steps (not run here): raise the r weight or constrain the fusion to keep v3's f/r ratio, or add the overlay/strings-augmented malware rows used for rf_adv to the ember_ft_v4 training. Then re-run this suite before any promotion.
